The fix is commit `cd6cf1f` (PR #1943, ticket O3-6093, "Improve support for arrow functions in expression variable extractor"). It is in `openmrs-esm-core`, author Ian.

The change replaces the old `isLocalExpression` flag with a `boundNames` set. Arrow-function parameters are added to that set and passed down into the body, so `x` is excluded there but `b` in `a.map(x => f(b))` is reported. The old code dropped the body's variables when they came back through the return value, which is why only `a` was reported. The new behaviour is covered by the test "extracts unbound variables from any kind of arrow function body" (`a.map(x => f(b))` now yields `['a', 'f', 'b']`).

Implementation in esm-core, all in `packages/framework/esm-expression-evaluator/src/`:
- `extractVariableNames()` creates the context and walks the expression. It is the public entry point, exported from `public.ts`.
- `visitArrowFunctionExpression()` collects the parameter names and visits the body with them bound. This is the core of the fix.
- `visitIdentifier()` only records a name if it is not a global and not in `boundNames`.
- `EvaluationContext` and `createContextInternal()` hold the new `boundNames` field in place of `isLocalExpression`.
- `visitMemberExpression()` no longer uses the local-expression flag. Only computed properties are visited.
